name: AI Agent Chat Layout
description: A chat layout for an AI assistant: an optional conversation list, a transcript that follows new content only while the reader is at the bottom, and a composer whose Send button turns into Stop while a reply streams. A message that fails to send stays in the input with a retry, and screen readers hear one status region instead of every token.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

layout.layering: The header and the composer are rows outside the scrolling transcript, so they need no z-index. Menus and popovers sit above the page, and toasts above those. Below 1024 px the conversation list is a modal: native <dialog> opened with showModal() is drawn in the top layer and makes the rest of the page inert.

positioningContract.page: A full-height grid, 100dvh tall with 100vh as the fallback: the conversation list column, when docked, and the chat column
positioningContract.header: The chat column's first row, outside the scrolling area
positioningContract.transcript: The chat column's scrolling area, between the header and the composer
positioningContract.composer: The chat column's last row, outside the scrolling area
positioningContract.sidebar: Its own grid column from 1024 px wide; a modal overlay below that

invariants: The header and the composer stay visible because they're outside the scrolling area, not because of position: fixed, so they never cover the focused element
In the chat column only the transcript scrolls, and a docked conversation list scrolls inside its own column, so neither stretches the page

Grid and flex items default to min-height: auto, so the page grid's columns get min-height: 0; without it, a long conversation list or conversation stretches the page and pushes the composer off screen
A docked conversation list takes its own column and never covers the chat
At 320 px wide nothing scrolls sideways, apart from code blocks, which scroll inside themselves

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend the shell of an AI chat: an optional conversation list, a header, the transcript, and the composer. Build on the project's chat, message, and input components when it has suitable ones; otherwise use plain HTML. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and add no dependency without asking. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA. Assistant messages go through the project's own renderer; the AI Response Rendering Pattern covers streaming, Markdown, and tool calls inside them, and the AI Action Review Pattern covers approving the assistant's actions.
keyFeatures: Built on the project's chat and input components, or on a plain form with a labelled textarea and one submit button

A full-height layout (dvh) whose header and composer sit outside the transcript's scrolling area, so they never cover the focused element or hide behind mobile toolbars, and a conversation list that scrolls on its own
Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line, never while an IME is composing; on touch-primary devices Enter adds a line by default
One button that turns into Stop while a reply streams and keeps focus; Enter keeps the draft until the reply ends
The draft stays in the composer until the server accepts the message, so a failed send shows Not sent with Retry and loses nothing
The transcript follows new content only while the reader is at the bottom; otherwise a Jump to latest button appears
A visually hidden heading starts each message, and one polite status region announces replies starting, ending, and failing, never the streamed text
A conversation list that is navigation: docked from 1024 px, a modal overlay below, and hidden when closed
Optional capabilities, each with when it helps: branching, pinning, history search, and keyboard shortcuts
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has chat, message, or composer components, configure or extend them to meet this guide instead of building others, and keep their APIs.
2. Choose what the task needs: the conversation list, attachments, quick actions, and the optional capabilities in commonVariations. Leave out the rest.
3. Lay out the page as layoutModel says: a full-height grid with the header and the composer outside the scrolling transcript.

4. Build the composer (components.Composer): the Enter rules, one Send and Stop button, and a draft that stays until the message is accepted (frameworkPatterns.composerEnterKey, sendStopButton, and sendMessage).

5. Render the transcript (components.Transcript and components.Message): each message starts with a visually hidden heading, the person's messages show their send status, and assistant messages go through the project's renderer.
6. Add the conversation's status region (accessibility.screenReader) and the scrolling rules (frameworkPatterns.pinnedToBottom).
7. If the task needs it, add the conversation list (components.Sidebar), with a skip link when it comes before the chat.
8. Save only the UI state the product needs, under the app's own storage prefix, and apply it before the first paint (stateManagement).
9. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, an input method editor, and a phone, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

ChatLayout.description: The page grid: a skip link when the conversation list comes first, the conversation list, and the chat column

SkipLink.description: The first focusable element when the docked list comes before the chat; moves focus to the chat

ChatColumn.description: The main region: header, transcript, and composer

Header.description: The conversation's title, the list toggle, and actions

Composer.description: A form with a textarea and one Send and Stop button

StatusRegion.description: One polite status region for the conversation, visually hidden and present from the start

Sidebar.description: Optional conversation list. It's navigation: a nav element labelled "Conversations", with a link for each conversation, since each conversation has its own URL.

elements.NewChatButton: At the top of the list. It starts a new conversation and puts focus in the composer.
elements.ConversationLinks: A list of links, the open conversation marked with aria-current="page". Optional groups, such as Today and Previous 7 days, get headings.
elements.ItemActions: Optional rename, pin, and delete, in a More actions menu button per item. Delete asks first (see the Dialog guide) or offers undo.
elements.Filter: Optional search field that filters the list; the number of matches is announced politely.

behavior.scroll: The list scrolls inside its column (overflow-y: auto) while docked, and inside the dialog in the overlay, so a long list never stretches the page.
behavior.docked: From 1024 px wide the list is a grid column, open by default. A toggle in the header opens and closes it: a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls. When closed, the column is hidden (the hidden attribute or display: none), not only moved off screen.
behavior.overlay: Below 1024 px the list opens as a modal: native <dialog> opened with showModal(), or the Dialog guide's model. It has a visible Close button, closes on Escape, on a backdrop click, and when a conversation is chosen, and returns focus to the toggle.
behavior.skipLink: When the docked list comes before the chat in the page, the page starts with a skip link to the chat (WCAG 2.4.1).
behavior.breakpointChange: React to a matchMedia change, not to resize events. If the overlay is open when the window gets wider than 1024 px, close it and move focus to the same item in the docked list.

elements.ListToggle: Shown when the conversation list can be opened or closed. Its name contains its visible text, if it has any, and it is at least 24 by 24 px.
elements.ConversationTitle: The conversation's title, as the page's main heading, or a visually hidden heading such as "Chat". document.title includes it.
elements.HeaderActions: Optional: New chat, an assistant or model picker, and a More actions menu. Clearing a conversation asks first or offers undo.

behavior.phones: The toggle, the title, and New chat; the other actions go in the More actions menu.

Transcript.description: The conversation, oldest first, in the chat column's scrolling area.

behavior.structure: A list or a series of articles, in reading order. It isn't a live region: replies are announced through the status region.
behavior.followingNewContent: Follow new content only while the reader is at the bottom (within 48 px). Only scrolling up stops following; content that grows below the view never does. Follow instantly, never with smooth scrolling. While the reader is scrolled up, show JumpToLatest. Sending a message scrolls to the bottom and follows again (frameworkPatterns.pinnedToBottom).
behavior.opening: A conversation opens at its latest message.
behavior.olderMessages: Loading older messages at the top keeps what's on screen where it is.

Message.description: One message, from the person or from the assistant.

elements.SpeakerHeading: A visually hidden heading at the start of each message, such as "You said:" or "Acme Assistant said:", one level below the conversation's heading. Screen reader users move between messages with the heading key. Don't put aria-label on a message: it would replace the content.
elements.Content: The person's messages are plain text with their line breaks (white-space: pre-wrap) and dir="auto". Assistant messages go through the project's renderer. Links in messages are underlined.
elements.SendStatus: The person's messages show sending, sent (or nothing), or failed: "Not sent" with a Retry button.
elements.Actions: Optional on the person's messages: Edit, which lets them change the message and send it again (see commonVariations.branching), and Copy. Every icon button has a name and is at least 24 by 24 px.
elements.Avatar: Optional and decorative (alt=""), since the heading names the speaker.
elements.Timestamp: Optional, in a time element with a datetime attribute.

behavior.alignment: The person's messages sit on the end side (right in left-to-right languages) and the assistant's on the start side. Logical properties, such as margin-inline-start, mirror the layout for right-to-left languages.
behavior.longContent: Long text wraps (overflow-wrap: anywhere). A code block scrolls inside itself; one that scrolls and has nothing focusable gets tabindex="0" and a name.

WaitingIndicator.description: Shown from the moment the message is accepted until the reply's first content appears (the queued state).

elements.Dots: Decorative (aria-hidden="true"), and static under reduced motion. The status region announces the start once.

behavior.hide: As soon as content appears, or when the reply's streaming cursor appears, if the project follows the AI Response Rendering Pattern.

Composer.description: A form with a textarea and one submit button, in the last row of the chat column.

elements.Textarea: Labelled; the label can be visually hidden. If a placeholder shows a prompt such as "Message Acme Assistant", the label uses the same words, so voice control users can say what they see. Text is at least 16 px, so iOS Safari doesn't zoom the page on focus. It grows with its content up to about 8 lines, then scrolls inside: field-sizing: content where the browser supports it, otherwise set the height from scrollHeight on input.
elements.SendStopButton: One button: Send, or Stop while a reply streams. It never gets the disabled attribute, which would drop focus to the page when its state changes. With nothing to send it has aria-disabled="true" and does nothing. Its name follows its state: "Send message" or "Stop response". In Stop mode it has formnovalidate, so a required field or other form validation never blocks Stop (frameworkPatterns.sendStopButton).
elements.AttachmentButton: Optional. Opens the file picker. Attached files show as chips with a remove button named for the file ("Remove report.csv").
elements.QuickActions: Optional buttons that fill the composer and move focus to it, so the person can edit before sending. Suggested prompts in an empty conversation may send at once when they need no editing.
elements.ComposerError: Text under the composer for problems with the draft, such as a message that's too long or a rejected file, linked to the textarea with aria-describedby.

behavior.enter: Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line. Enter that confirms an input method editor (IME) composition never sends: check isComposing, and keyCode 229, which is how Safari reports that Enter. When the primary input is touch ((hover: none) and (pointer: coarse)), assume an on-screen keyboard, which has no Shift+Enter, so Enter adds a line and the button sends. This is a heuristic: a tablet with a keyboard may get the new-line default, and touchscreen laptops usually keep Enter to send. An existing Enter-to-send setting overrides it, and the button always sends (frameworkPatterns.composerEnterKey).
behavior.whileReplyStreams: The button turns into Stop, which stops the reply and keeps its text. The textarea stays editable, so the next message can be drafted, but Enter doesn't send until the reply ends or is stopped.
behavior.sending: The message appears in the transcript as sending, and the draft stays in the composer until the server accepts the message. It leaves only if the composer still holds the sent text, so anything typed meanwhile stays. The button is ignored while a message is being sent, so a double press sends once (frameworkPatterns.sendMessage).
behavior.failure: The message shows "Not sent" with Retry, the draft is still in the composer, and the status region says "Message not sent". Retry sends the message again with the same id, so the server can drop a copy it already has, as when a dropped connection hid that the first attempt arrived. Sending a changed draft instead replaces the failed message.
behavior.focus: Sending doesn't move focus: after Enter it stays in the textarea, and after a press of the button it stays on the button. Don't focus the composer when the page loads on touch devices, where that opens the on-screen keyboard; focus it when the person starts a new conversation or picks a suggested prompt.
behavior.escape: Optional: Escape in the composer stops a streaming reply, unless the chat sits in a dialog or panel that Escape closes.

EmptyState.description: Shown in a conversation with no messages.

elements.Heading: A short heading, such as "How can I help?"

JumpToLatest.description: A button at the bottom of the transcript, shown while the reader is scrolled up.

behavior.activate: Scrolls to the bottom, follows new content again, and puts focus in the composer, since the button hides itself.

desktop.sidebar: Docked column, open by default, toggled from the header

tablet.transcript: Full width with 24 px side padding

mobile.transcript: Full width with 16 px side padding
mobile.targets: At least 24 by 24 px; 44 px is comfortable for touch

resizeHandling.approach: React to changes of matchMedia('(min-width: 1024px)'), not to resize events; see components.Sidebar.behavior.breakpointChange.

draft.persistence: Optional: per conversation, in sessionStorage or where the app keeps drafts, under the app's own prefix; cleared once the message is sent

sending.description: Whether a message is being sent; the button is ignored meanwhile.

replyState.description: The lifecycle of the current reply (the AI Response Rendering Pattern uses the same states). The button is Stop while the reply is queued, streaming, running a tool, or awaiting review.

pinnedToBottom.description: Whether the transcript follows new content.

sidebarOpen.description: Whether the docked conversation list is open. The overlay always starts closed.
sidebarOpen.persistence: Optional: a cookie the server reads, or storage under the app's own prefix (for example acme.chat.sidebar, where acme stands for the app's prefix), applied by a small inline script before the first paint, so the layout doesn't jump

activeConversationId.persistence: router/URL: each conversation has its own URL

ssrConsiderations.transcript: With server rendering, render the conversation on the server, so it shows before scripts run.
ssrConsiderations.savedState: Apply the saved state of the docked list before the first paint, with a cookie or a small inline script, as dark mode does for the theme.

navigationBehavior.onConversationChange: The overlay closes and the transcript opens at the latest message. In a single-page app, focus moves to the conversation's heading (tabindex="-1") and document.title changes.
navigationBehavior.replyInProgress: Switching conversations doesn't stop a reply on the server. It shows when the person returns, never in the conversation they switched to.
navigationBehavior.drafts: Drafts are kept per conversation, so switching back restores one.

messageAlignment.user: end: right in left-to-right languages, left in right-to-left ones
messageAlignment.assistant: start: left in left-to-right languages, right in right-to-left ones

rtl.notes: Use logical properties (margin-inline-start, padding-inline, inset-inline-end) and dir on the root, so the layout mirrors without separate styles. dir="auto" on the person's messages shows mixed-direction text correctly.

mobileSafeArea.notes: Pad the header's top and the composer's bottom with env(safe-area-inset-top) and env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and add viewport-fit=cover to the viewport meta tag. Add interactive-widget=resizes-content to the same tag, so browsers that support it, such as Chrome on Android, shrink the layout when the on-screen keyboard opens and the composer stays above it. iOS Safari keeps the layout size and scrolls the focused field into view.

messageEnter.notes: opacity 0 to 1 and translateY(4px) to none, only for messages that arrive while the page is open, never for the history on load

sidebarSlide.notes: The docked list slides in from the start side

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing slides or fades, and the waiting dots are static.

requirements.1.3.1: Each message starts with a heading that names the speaker, the conversation list is a nav, and the composer has a label.
requirements.1.4.3: Text, including placeholders and timestamps, has at least 4.5:1 contrast.
requirements.1.4.10: At 320 px wide nothing scrolls sideways, apart from code blocks that scroll inside themselves.
requirements.1.4.11: The composer's edge, icons, and focus indicators have at least 3:1 contrast.
requirements.1.4.12: Bubbles and buttons use min-height and padding, not fixed heights, so larger text spacing doesn't cut them off.
requirements.2.1.1: Everything works from the keyboard, including Jump to latest and every message action.
requirements.2.4.1: When the conversation list comes before the chat, a skip link moves past it.
requirements.2.4.3: Sending doesn't move focus, and closing the overlay returns focus to the toggle.
requirements.2.4.7: Every control shows a visible focus indicator (:focus-visible).
requirements.2.4.11: The header and the composer are outside the scrolling area, so they never cover the focused element.
requirements.2.5.3: Each control's name contains its visible text, and the composer's label contains its placeholder's words.
requirements.2.5.8: Controls are at least 24 by 24 CSS px.
requirements.3.3.1: A failed send and a draft that's too long are described in text.
requirements.4.1.2: The button's name follows its state, and aria-disabled="true" says when there is nothing to send.
requirements.4.1.3: Replies starting, ending, and failing, and failed sends, are announced through one polite status region without moving focus.

keyboardNavigation.escape: Closes the conversation overlay and menus. Optional: see components.Composer.behavior.escape.
keyboardNavigation.tabOrder: The skip link, the docked conversation list, the header, the controls in the transcript, then the composer.

listToggle.aria-expanded: true or false, for the docked list

composerTextarea.label: A label element, or aria-label, that contains the placeholder's words
composerTextarea.aria-describedby: The composer's error text, while it shows

sendStopButton.name: "Send message" or "Stop response"
sendStopButton.aria-disabled: "true" while there is nothing to send

statusRegion.notes: Visually hidden, present before anything changes, one per conversation

listToggle.aria-haspopup: "dialog", when it opens the overlay; never "true", which announces a menu

announcements.neverAnnounced: The streamed text, and the person's own message

screenReader.findingReplies: After "Response complete", people find the reply by its heading.
screenReader.modals: A modal over the chat, such as the conversation overlay, makes the status region inert, which hides it from screen readers. Anything that must be heard while a modal is open goes through a status region inside it.

focusManagement.onLoad: Don't focus the composer when the page loads on touch devices.
focusManagement.overlay: Opening it moves focus into the list; closing it returns focus to the toggle.

colorContrast.requirement: 4.5:1 for text; 3:1 for the composer's edge, icons, and focus indicators
colorContrast.check: Check the project's own colors, including on the person's bubbles and in dark mode.

designSystem.note: Suggested defaults for projects without a design. The project's tokens and existing components win; check its colors meet the same contrast.

light.userBubble: #2563eb with #ffffff text (5.2:1); links in it underlined in the text color
light.assistantText: #111827 (17.7:1); assistant messages can do without a bubble
light.mutedText: #6b7280 (4.8:1), for timestamps, statuses, and the placeholder

typography.code: The project's monospace font at 14 px

designSystem.notes: Bubble tails and shadows are optional decoration; the side and the speaker heading tell messages apart.

message.description: One message. Adapt the field names to the project, and keep their meaning.

fields.status: The person's messages: sending, sent, or failed. Assistant messages use the reply's lifecycle (stateManagement.statesToTrack.replyState).

conversation.description: One entry in the conversation list.

commonVariations.withoutSidebar: A single conversation, or a conversation picker in the header.
commonVariations.embeddedChat: A launcher button opens the chat in a modal dialog (see the Dialog guide) or a side panel. A panel moves focus in when it opens, closes with Escape, returns focus to the launcher, and leaves the page usable.
commonVariations.multipleAssistants: Each assistant message's heading names its assistant.
commonVariations.branching: Optional. Helps when people edit an earlier question and expect the original answer kept. Editing creates a new version of the message, which shows "2 of 3" with Previous and Next version buttons; the transcript below follows the chosen version. Announce the change.
commonVariations.pinning: Optional. Helps when people return to a few conversations often. Pinned conversations sit in their own group at the top of the list.
commonVariations.historySearch: Optional. Helps when people ask where an earlier conversation went. A search over all conversations, with results that link to the conversation and its matching message. Announce the number of results.
commonVariations.keyboardShortcuts: Optional. Helps people who chat all day, for example with a shortcut for New chat and one to the composer. Avoid keys the browser and screen readers use, list the shortcuts in the interface, and let people turn off single-key shortcuts (WCAG 2.1.4).

implementationDetails.assistantMessages: Assistant messages go through the project's renderer. With the AI Response Rendering Pattern, this layout owns the shell, the Send and Stop button, Edit on the person's messages, following new content, and the conversation's status region; the pattern owns the inside of each assistant message, including Copy, Regenerate, and feedback, and announces through this layout's status region.
implementationDetails.actions: With the AI Action Review Pattern, this layout places the review: a card in the transcript for low-risk actions, or a side panel, drawer, or dialog for the rest.
implementationDetails.statusRegion: One element with role="status" per conversation, visually hidden and present before anything changes, holding one short sentence at a time.
implementationDetails.attachments: Type and size checks in the browser are a convenience; the server checks them again. Show file names as text.
implementationDetails.performance: Virtualize the transcript only when conversations get long (several hundred messages), and keep the newest messages and any focused element rendered. Update streaming content at most once per animation frame.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version. form, textarea, button, transcript, and jumpButton stand for the composer's and the transcript's elements; conversation, sendMessage(), showMessage(), and announce() stand for the app's state, its request, its transcript, and the status region.

composerEnterKey.description: Enter in the composer, as components.Composer.behavior.enter says.

sendStopButton.description: The composer's one button, Send or Stop: never disabled, and in Stop mode never blocked by form validation.

sendMessage.description: Sending: the draft stays until the server accepts the message, a double press sends once, each message has an id that Retry reuses, and the Stop button stops the reply.

pinnedToBottom.description: Following new content only at the bottom, with Jump to latest.

edgeCases.doubleSend: The button is ignored while a message is being sent, so a double press or a held Enter sends once.
edgeCases.offline: A send while offline fails like any other, with Not sent and Retry. Optionally, retry once the browser is back online, and say so.
edgeCases.replyDoesNotStart: Give the request a time limit, for example 30 seconds, and show the failure with Retry when it runs out. Tell a timeout from other failures by the signal's reason, as the Dialog guide does.
edgeCases.longDraft: If the product limits message length, show the count near the limit and explain an over-limit draft under the composer. Never cut the draft.
edgeCases.reload: After a reload during a reply, show what the server saved, and continue the stream if the backend supports it.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

must: Build on the project's chat, message, and input components when they're suitable, and keep their APIs
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
Implement only the parts and options the task needs
Keep the draft in the composer until the server accepts the message
Keep one Send and Stop button that changes state without losing focus
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a chat UI kit, an autosize library, or a focus-trap library, without asking
Send while an IME is composing text
Put the disabled attribute on the Send and Stop button
Put aria-label on messages, or make the transcript a live region that reads streamed text
Move the transcript while the reader is scrolled up, or follow new content with smooth scrolling
Use position: fixed for the header or the composer over a scrolling page
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line; Enter that confirms an IME composition (Japanese, Chinese, Korean) doesn't send, including in Safari
With a phone's on-screen keyboard, Enter adds a line and the button sends; an Enter-to-send setting overrides that on every device
While a reply streams, the button is Stop and keeps focus, form validation never blocks it, Stop keeps the reply's text, and Enter in the composer keeps the draft without sending
With nothing to send, the button is aria-disabled, stays focusable, and does nothing
A message that fails to send shows Not sent with Retry, the draft is still in the composer, and a screen reader hears that it wasn't sent
A draft typed while a message is being sent stays in the composer, and a double press sends once
The transcript follows new content only at the bottom; scrolled up, it stays put, and Jump to latest scrolls down and puts focus in the composer
A screen reader can move between messages by heading, hears that a reply started and ended, and never hears the streamed text
The header and the composer never cover the focused element, and on phones the composer stays above the browser's toolbars and the on-screen keyboard
With a long conversation list and a long conversation, each scrolls on its own, and the composer stays on screen
Below 1024 px the conversation list opens as a modal with a Close button, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the toggle; a closed list can't be reached with Tab
The open conversation has aria-current and is named in the page title, and a skip link moves past a long conversation list
At 320 px wide and at 400% zoom nothing scrolls sideways, and right-to-left languages mirror the layout
With reduced motion, nothing slides or fades, and following new content never animates
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens, and text, the composer's edge, and focus indicators meet the contrast minimums

relatedPotions.description: Optional: what goes inside an assistant message: streaming, Markdown, tool calls, citations, and per-message controls. This layout owns the shell, the Send and Stop button, Edit on the person's messages, following new content, and the status region; the pattern owns the inside of each assistant message. Hide the waiting indicator when its streaming cursor appears.
Optional: approving the actions the assistant proposes. This layout places the review, as a card in the transcript or in a side panel; the pattern owns everything in it.
Optional: for the conversation overlay below 1024 px, and for confirmations such as deleting a conversation.
Optional: when the conversation list sits next to the app's own navigation.
Optional: quick prompts, commands, and switching conversations from the keyboard.
Optional: label, hint, and error conventions for the composer.
Optional: for feedback outside the conversation, such as a deleted conversation with Undo.
Optional: for an assistant or model picker.
Optional: when the chat sits under the site's own header.
Optional: for the composer's button and the header's actions.
